description: The Global Coal Plant Tracker from Global Energy Monitor (GEM), a non-profit research organisation, catalogues coal-fired power units worldwide: every unit of 30 MW or more that is operating, proposed since 2010 or retired since 2000. On 26 September 2026 the page counted 14,674 units in 111 countries with more than 3,000 plant owners. The database records each unit's owner and parent company, status, plant and coal type, combustion technology, capacity, location and estimated carbon dioxide emissions, and each power station has a footnoted GEM.wiki page with project history. Data are updated twice a year, around January and July; the latest release was July 2026. Coverage is global. Access is through a free online tracker map, dashboards and summary tables, and the full data set is a spreadsheet downloadable through a short download form on GEM's site, under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: units under 30 MW are excluded, and status and emissions are researcher estimates from public sources. Simulation uses are hazard exposure of thermal generation, retirement and capacity planning scenarios and cooling-water or heat risk screening. Related records: data-gem-global-integrated-power-tracker combines GEM's power trackers and data-gem-global-energy-ownership-tracker maps owners.
